haiku-low.q1: Keys load at startup, before readiness. GET /healthz returns 200 only after all three keys are loaded, so no traffic goes to a pod without them.
haiku-low.q2: It retries 3 times, 2 seconds apart, then exits non-zero. The new pod never becomes ready, the rollout halts, and old pods keep serving live traffic.
haiku-low.q3: Every 5 minutes it re-reads the three keys and swaps in any changed version in memory. If the read fails, it keeps the last good value, logs a warning, and retries at the next tick.
haiku-low.q4: Key values live only in process memory. They must never go to disk, environment variables, or logs. Logging version ids is fine.
haiku-low.q5: Only the orders-api-prod service identity reads prod values, read-only. Only the security on-call writes them. Engineers cannot read prod values.
haiku-low.q6: Git history is not rewritten, and images built earlier still contain the keys, so they are treated as leaked. Rotating and then revoking the old keys at each provider makes them harmless.
haiku-low.q7: Each provider client calls secrets.get(name) on every request instead of copying the key at construction, so a refreshed value reaches the clients without a restart.
haiku-low.q8: The team waits until all 4 replicas show the new version id in /healthz, which can take up to one 5-minute refresh. Only then is the old key revoked.
haiku-low.q9: Set store access, copy current keys into the store, switch the app to read from the store, remove keys from the committed config, then rotate and revoke keys at providers.
haiku-low.q10: make run sets APP_ENV=dev and reads orders-api/dev/* sandbox keys, using the developer's dev read access. Developers never need prod access to run locally.

sonnet.q1: Keys are loaded first (from the store, at startup); /healthz returns 200 and the pod becomes ready only after all three keys are loaded.
sonnet.q2: It retries 3 times, 2 seconds apart, then exits non-zero. It never becomes ready, so the rollout halts and old pods keep serving traffic.
sonnet.q3: Every 5 minutes the app re-reads the three keys; if a version changed, the new value replaces the old in memory and the new version id is logged. If a re-read fails, it keeps the last good value, logs a warning, retries at the next 5-minute tick, and keeps serving.
sonnet.q4: Held only in process memory. They must never go to disk, environment variables, or logs (version ids may be logged).
sonnet.q5: Read: the orders-api-prod service identity (read-only on orders-api/prod/*); engineers cannot read prod values. Write: only the security on-call.
sonnet.q6: The keys remain in git history (not rewritten) and in old container images, so they are treated as leaked. Rotating them at the provider and then revoking the old keys makes the old values harmless.
sonnet.q7: Each provider client calls secrets.get(name) on every request rather than copying the key at construction, so a refreshed in-memory value is used without a restart.
sonnet.q8: Wait until all 4 replicas show the new version id in /healthz (up to one 5-minute refresh); only then revoke. If any replica doesn't show it, don't revoke.
sonnet.q9: 1) Set store access; 2) copy current keys into the store; 3) write code to read from the store and 4) remove keys from config (same merge); then 5-6) deploy/verify; 7) rotate keys at providers (then revoke old ones).
sonnet.q10: From the store's orders-api/dev/* sandbox keys (make run sets APP_ENV=dev), using the developer's own dev read access; no prod access or live keys.
sonnet.q11: NOT STATED (listed as an open question: undecided whether a missing key follows the retry-then-exit rule).
sonnet.q12: No schedule is set; the plan sets no cadence and security has not decided whether or how often to rotate regularly.
